stem: Jasper is a 2-year-old boy with fever, hypoxia, raised inflammatory markers, and chest x-ray showing right lower lobe collapse and consolidation consistent with bacterial pneumonia. What treatment will you commence?
explanation: This presentation is most consistent with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia with lobar consolidation in a mildly hypoxic child who can be treated with oral antibiotics if otherwise stable. Amoxicillin-clavulanate (Augmentin) provides appropriate cover for common bacterial respiratory pathogens, including beta-lactamase–producing organisms.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The options already included a suitable first-line oral antibiotic choice, so the question can be preserved and answered as a single-best-answer item.

optionExplanations.A: Appropriate oral treatment for uncomplicated bacterial pneumonia in a stable child.
optionExplanations.B: Macrolide therapy is mainly used when atypical pathogens are suspected; this is less likely in a 2-year-old with lobar consolidation.
optionExplanations.C: Benzylpenicillin is not the best first-line choice here for community-acquired lobar pneumonia.
optionExplanations.D: Flucloxacillin is used for staphylococcal infection, which is not the best fit for this presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Ceftriaxone may be used for severe pneumonia or when oral therapy is not suitable, but it is not first choice here.
